answer: Stake-bonded reputation makes each identity expensive to forge: an agent locks a deposit before trading, slashed if peers catch it running duplicate accounts. Like a wharf charging every ship a berth fee before it may dock, the bond prices fakes out of the harbor. A public lantern of past behavior — trades, disputes, uptime — lets others check history before trusting, so a fresh copy starts at zero trust. Forging a record costs time and stake per fake, while honest agents keep their bond and build standing; attacker cost scales with every fake, but each check stays cheap.
